motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: Things that land: capsule scale, check, swatch lift, switch thumb.

motion.name: dur-1
motion.purpose: Hover and press feedback.

motion.name: dur-2
motion.purpose: State changes (Calm: 1ms).

motion.name: dur-3
motion.purpose: Colour and settle transitions (Calm: 120ms).

motion.name: spring-arc
motion.purpose: Arc start/end angles and radii; always the nearest turn. Instant under Calm.

motion.name: arc-bloom
motion.value: first paint only: delay 120ms + 55ms × index, arcs grow from zero sweep
motion.purpose: A fresh dial blooms clockwise, arc by arc.

motion.name: arc-lift
motion.purpose: Spring-driven radius lift.

motion.name: hand-step
motion.value: transform 0.8s ease-out; steps every 60s (every 5s on 60-minute faces)
motion.purpose: Now-hand; idle repaint at most once a minute on hour-scale dials.

motion.name: seconds-bead
motion.value: HTML layer, rotate stepped from the wall clock each second, transition 0.28s ease-out
motion.purpose: Never a free-running CSS animation. Hidden under Calm.

motion.name: aura
motion.value: opacity 0.12 → 0.70 → 0.12, 8s ease-in-out infinite (4s during heads-up); static at 0.35 under Calm
motion.purpose: The only always-on loop: the block under the hand breathes. HTML conic-gradient layer with a static ring mask; only opacity animates.

motion.name: breathing-guide
motion.value: transform scale 0.45 → 1 + opacity, 16s cycle (4 in · 4 hold · 6 out · 2 rest), runs 64s
motion.purpose: User-started one-minute pause in the face.

motion.name: liquid-level
motion.value: transform translateY, 0.9s ease-out, updates once a minute
motion.purpose: Live rail capsule fill.

motion.name: wave-slosh
motion.value: translateX(-20px): strip A 1.6s ×2, strip B 2.7s ×1 reverse, remounted each minute; linear infinite only while hovered; none under Calm
motion.purpose: The liquid surface sloshes once per minute, then rests.

motion.name: now-ping
motion.purpose: Rail now-dot as the minute turns; none under Calm.

motion.name: lume-charge
motion.value: stroke-dashoffset sweep 0.95s cubic-bezier(0.3, 0.7, 0.2, 1), soft-light white band, once
motion.purpose: A finished arc charges with light.

motion.name: day-sweep
motion.value: lume band around the bezel 2.4s cubic-bezier(0.45, 0.05, 0.2, 1), plus-lighter, once
motion.purpose: Every block of the day done.

motion.name: pour
motion.value: liquid to brim 1.3s ease-out then fade; icon and check pop 0.45–0.5s
motion.purpose: Rail block finished. Skipped under Calm.

motion.name: strike-draw
motion.purpose: Finished title strike draws left to right.

motion.name: day-turn
motion.purpose: Changing day turns the dial in the direction of travel.

motion.name: odometer
motion.value: per character translateY 55% + blur 2px, 420ms cubicOut; crossfade 260ms when the text changes shape
motion.purpose: Countdown and tally digits.

motion.name: theme-reveal
motion.value: View Transition, clip-path circle from the clicked swatch, 650ms ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Theme and light/dark switch. Skipped under Calm.

motion.name: segmented-thumb
motion.purpose: Reference switcher thumb glide.

motion.name: week-puck
motion.purpose: Selected-day puck in the week strip.

motion.name: panel-fly
motion.purpose: Inspector panel.

motion.name: toast-rise
motion.value: in: y 16px 280ms cubicOut · countdown bar scaleX linear over the undo window
motion.purpose: Toasts from the rail foot.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Tactile press on :active.

narrative.overview:
Daybloom is one object sitting on a quiet desk. The object is a Bauhaus watch dial: Max-Bill-thin numerals, a minute track, and a bezel whose coloured inserts are the day's blocks. You plan by sweeping the bezel, not by filling in forms. Everything else (the top bar, the day rail, the inspector panel, the settings) is the desk it rests on. The desk is cool, low in contrast, and tonally layered so the dial is always the first thing you read. The system rejects the category default of a calendar grid with a clock pasted beside it. Time is drawn as angle and area, and every number on screen has a shape that says the same thing faster.

Colour is semantic before it is decorative. Seven category colours carry meaning on every surface. One signal colour means *now*. One lume colour means *finished*. Free time keeps the bare neutral of the bezel. The palette is calm on purpose. Its users experience time blindness and anxiety around transitions, so nothing is red, nothing flashes, and nothing loops except one slow breathing halo around the block you are in. Delight is spent on real progress: a block draws itself onto the bezel, a finished block glows with lume, and a capsule fills like a glass.

The world ships as ten whole-app themes (four light, six dark, including true black). Each theme pairs with one of nine dial finishes. The planner, the desktop widget and the dial always agree.
keyCharacteristics: A 1000-unit SVG dial with fixed radii: bezel band, minute track, numeral ring and face, all drawn in the finish's colours.
Seven-colour categorical palette, with a light value and a lifted dark value per category, chosen by the dial finish.
Cool tonal desk (ground, surface, raised, sunken). Elevation is mostly tone, plus three soft shadows.
Lexend Variable throughout. Weight 300 for dial lettering, 500 as the ceiling for chrome. Tabular numerals for every time.
Pills and circles for controls, gently rounded rectangles for containers, annular sectors for time.
Springs for arc geometry, ease-out tokens for chrome. Continuous motion is compositor-only and stops under Calm.

rules.name: The Category Is the Meaning Rule
rules.body: A block's colour is its category, on every surface: dial insert, rail capsule, quick-add icon tint, chip dot, category picker, the inspector's 4px accent stripe and the breathing aura. Never colour a block by status, priority or source.

rules.name: The Signal Means Now Rule
rules.body: Signal marks the present moment and the place you are acting on right now. It is never decoration, never a category, and never a button fill.

rules.name: The Lume Means Done Rule
rules.body: Lume is the reward colour. It is spent only on finished time, plus the watch-native luminous indices on dark dials.

rules.name: The Free Time Is Bare Rule
rules.body: Unplanned time is never painted. On the dial it is bare bezel, showing faint graduation dots (track colour at 45%). In the rail it is a dotted Firm Hairline with Pencil Grey "45m free" text. In the time-timer face it is a wedge of track mixed into the face, tipped with a 4° edge in the next block's colour.

rules.name: The Tabular Time Rule
rules.body: Every time, duration, count and countdown uses tabular numerals: the `.tnum` utility or `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`. Digits never shift width as time passes, and changing digits roll like an odometer rather than reflow.

rules.name: The Thin Dial Rule
rules.body: Dial lettering is weight 300. Chrome is 400 to 500. Weight 600 is reserved for tiny 10.5–12px pill labels (the now-time pill and the toast action), where thin strokes would break up. There are no uppercase eyebrows or kickers. Hierarchy comes from size, weight and the ink ramp.

rules.name: The Dial First Rule
rules.body: Nothing covers the dial. The inspector panel slides in beside it as a non-modal inspector (fixed 64px from the top, 12px from the right), so the dial stays live. Toasts rise from the foot of the rail, 16px from the corner. Editing never dims the screen behind a scrim.

rules.name: The Tonal Desk Rule
rules.body: Reach for a tone step (sunken hover, raised selection) before a shadow. A shadow means the thing is held above the desk: selected, dragged, or a transient overlay.

rules.name: The Glow Is Not Elevation Rule
rules.body: Lume glow marks finished time, and nothing else may glow.

rules.name: The Lanes Only Where It Overlaps Rule
rules.body: The bezel splits into lanes only inside a cluster of blocks that actually overlap. Lanes are up to 3, with 5-unit gaps, outermost first. Every block outside a cluster keeps the full 86-unit band. Above two lanes, titles drop and icons carry the label.

rules.name: The Whole Word Rule
rules.body: Arc titles are fitted word by word into the room left after the icon. If fewer than three characters fit, no title is drawn and the icon stands alone. Never truncate with an ellipsis on the dial: a stub like "Lun…" reads worse than the icon.

rules.name: The Upright Label Rule
rules.body: Text reads clockwise from the start when it lands on the top half. When both the start and end of the words fall between 90° and 270°, the text runs counter-clockwise from the end, so it is never upside down. Its baseline moves from just inside the mid-radius (−0.36 em) to just outside (+0.36 em).

rules.name: The Hand Never Covers a Number Rule
rules.body: The thick part of the now-hand stays between the numerals and the bezel. Only a hairline crosses the inserts, so no numeral or label is ever hidden by the present.

rules.name: The Never-Red Rule
rules.body: A missed block fades toward the bezel and gets a dashed outline, and is offered a slide into the next free gap. Red is reserved for destructive actions and system errors, never for the user's time. There is no streak, no warning colour and no shaming state.

rules.name: The Compositor-Only Loop Rule
rules.body: Anything that moves without the user touching it animates only `opacity` or `transform` on an HTML layer. That covers the aura, the seconds bead, the liquid level, the waves and the now-ping. Never loop an animation on SVG geometry, a mask or a gradient. SVG may animate only in one-shots that end: the bloom, the charge, the day sweep and the wedge's path transition.

rules.name: The One Loop Rule
rules.body: The breathing aura is the only always-on loop. Everything else either steps with the clock (the hand once a minute, the bead once a second, the liquid once a minute) or plays once. The liquid wave sloshes once per minute, then rests.

rules.name: The Calm Switch Rule
rules.body: `prefers-reduced-motion`, or the in-app Motion setting set to Calm, sets `data-motion="calm"`. That turns every loop off. The aura holds still at 35%, and the waves, pings, seconds bead, sparks and pour are removed. Springs jump to their targets, Svelte transitions get zero duration, view transitions are skipped, and `--dur-2` and `--dur-3` collapse to 1ms and 120ms.

dos: **Do** paint every block in its category colour on every surface. Pick the light or lifted dark value from the dial finish's darkness (`categoryColor(id, finish.dark)`).
**Do** keep signal for now: the hand, the now-line, today's date, the caret and the drop target.
**Do** keep lume for finished time, and for luminous hour indices on dark dials.
**Do** leave free time bare: bezel graduation dots on the dial, a dotted Firm Hairline with "Nm free" in the rail.
**Do** give every block an icon and a label as well as a colour. Colour is never the only signal.
**Do** set every time, duration and count in tabular numerals.
**Do** draw dial geometry from the fixed radii in `geometry.ts` (bezel 468→382, track 366→340, numerals 298). Do not invent new rings.
**Do** animate arc geometry with springs (0.14 / 0.72) and chrome with the `--ease-*` and `--dur-*` tokens.
**Do** pair every new theme with a dial finish in the single `THEMES` table, so the planner, the widget and the dial agree.
**Do** gate every loop and every spatial transition behind `prefers-reduced-motion` and the Calm setting.
donts: **Don't** paint missed or overdue time red, or add any warning state. Missed blocks fade and dash.
**Don't** truncate a dial label with an ellipsis. Show whole words or the icon alone.
**Don't** let the now-hand's thick stroke cross the numerals or the bezel inserts. Only the hairline crosses.
**Don't** split the bezel into lanes for blocks that do not overlap, and don't exceed three lanes.
**Don't** loop an animation on SVG paths, masks or gradients. Don't add a second always-on loop beyond the breathing aura.
**Don't** use signal as a button, link or emphasis colour. The primary action is ink.
**Don't** cover the dial: no modal scrims for editing, and no toasts over the dial or its controls.
**Don't** use uppercase eyebrows or kickers. Section headings are 13px weight 500 Pencil Grey in sentence case.
**Don't** add hard or coloured shadows. Use the three soft ink shadows. Glow belongs to lume only.
